Kernel-Power 41 BugcheckCode: what the number means

Event 41 writes the stop code in decimal. Every guide and every Microsoft page uses hex. That is why 159 looks like nothing until you convert it.

By Marcin Firmuga·Published 2026-11-27·7 min read
Short answer

BugcheckCode in Event 41 is the blue screen code in decimal. 159 is 0x9F (DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE), 292 is 0x124 (WHEA_UNCORRECTABLE_ERROR), 278 is 0x116 (VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE). 0 means no stop code was written: a power loss, a hard hang, or the power button held. Type your number below.

Read the fields of Event 41

Open Event Viewer, Windows Logs, System, and double-click the Kernel-Power 41 entry. On the Details tab you see:

  • BugcheckCode: the stop code in decimal. Microsoft's own page on Event 41 says so: the code is decimal, while documentation uses hexadecimal.
  • BugcheckParameter1–4: extra data for that code. They matter in a debugger, less to you.
  • PowerButtonTimestamp: not zero means the power button was pressed and held.
  • SleepInProgress: whether the PC was going to sleep or waking when it stopped.

Microsoft describes three cases. A code that is not zero: Windows stopped with a blue screen, and the code says which. The power button: you held it. Zero everywhere, or no Event 41 at all: Windows could not write anything, which points at power (the power supply, the cable, the outlet) or a hang hard enough to stop writing to disk.

The codes that matter on a gaming PC

DecimalHexMicrosoft nameWhat it usually points at
0-(none)No stop code was written: a power loss, a hard hang, or the power button held. Check PowerButtonTimestamp. →
100xAIRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUALA driver touched memory it should not have at that moment. Usually a driver, sometimes unstable RAM. →
260x1AMEMORY_MANAGEMENTWindows found its memory management in a broken state. Test RAM and XMP or EXPO first. →
300x1EKMODE_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLEDA kernel-mode program raised an error nothing caught. The dump names the driver.
590x3BSYSTEM_SERVICE_EXCEPTIONAn error while running a system routine, often caused by a driver. The dump names it.
800x50PAGE_FAULT_IN_NONPAGED_AREAWindows referenced memory that was not there. RAM, a driver, or antivirus. →
1260x7ESYSTEM_THREAD_EXCEPTION_NOT_HANDLEDA system thread raised an error nothing caught. Usually a driver.
1270x7FUNEXPECTED_KERNEL_MODE_TRAPThe CPU raised a trap the kernel could not handle. Often hardware, heat or an overclock. →
1590x9FDRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILUREA driver was in an invalid power state, typically around sleep, wake or shutdown.
2090xD1DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUALA driver accessed paged or invalid memory at too high a priority. The dump names it.
2390xEFCRITICAL_PROCESS_DIEDA process Windows cannot run without stopped. Check the system drive and Windows files. →
2440xF4CRITICAL_OBJECT_TERMINATIONA critical process or thread ended. Often the system drive or its connection. →
2570x101CLOCK_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUTOne CPU core stopped answering. Overclock, undervolt or CPU instability. →
2650x109CRITICAL_STRUCTURE_CORRUPTIONWindows found kernel code or data changed. A driver or failing memory. →
2780x116VIDEO_TDR_FAILUREThe graphics driver hung and the reset failed, so Windows stopped. A GPU timeout that did not recover. →
2920x124WHEA_UNCORRECTABLE_ERRORThe hardware reported an error it could not correct (WHEA-Logger Event 18). →
3070x133DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATIONA driver routine ran too long. Often storage, network or graphics drivers, or drive firmware. →
3130x139KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILUREThe kernel found a corrupted data structure. A driver, memory or system files.

Some entries show a very large number, such as 268435582. That is 0x1000007E: the same stop code as 0x7E with an extra flag bit. Convert it and drop the leading 1.

Event 6008 and Event 1001: the companions

  • Event 6008 (source EventLog): "The previous system shutdown at … was unexpected." Windows writes it on the next start. It gives you the exact time; it never gives the cause.
  • Event 1001 (source BugCheck): "The computer has rebooted from a bugcheck. The bugcheck was: 0x…" When it is there, the stop code is in hex already, and a dump file usually sits in C:\Windows\Minidump.
  • Event 41 (Kernel-Power): written at the start after a dirty shutdown, with the BugcheckCode in decimal.

Filter the System log by 41,6008,1001. Three entries with the same minute are one event seen three ways. Then look at what came before that minute: a WHEA warning, a driver reset, a disk error.

Short answers

What does BugcheckCode 159 mean?

159 is 0x9F, DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE: a driver was in an invalid power state, usually around sleep, wake or shutdown.

What does BugcheckCode 0 mean?

No stop code was written. Microsoft lists a power problem, a hard hang or the power button. Check PowerButtonTimestamp and the power supply.

Why is the BugcheckCode in decimal?

Event 41 stores it that way. Microsoft's documentation uses hex, so convert it: 159 is 0x9F, 292 is 0x124.

What is the difference between Event 41 and 6008?

Both are written after an unexpected shutdown. 6008 gives the time; 41 adds the stop code if there was one. Neither is the cause.
